items.review_rationale: Read the equivalence radical(I)=m and m-primary for an ideal in a Noetherian local ring. Preserved the radical and primary-ideal notions as contextual unassigned references and did not confuse an ideal of definition with an arbitrary m-contained ideal.

references.phrase: local ring with maximal ideal m

references.context: Commutative algebra: ideal radical consisting of elements with a positive power in I
Commutative algebra: primary ideal with radical equal to maximal ideal m

references.disposition: The two criteria refer to the same ideal I, without claiming every proper ideal has radical m.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed inverse images of all quasi-compact open subsets of S and the equivalent test on affine open subsets. The quasi-compactness is of the preimage, not necessarily of X or of S globally.

references.phrase: inverse image f^{-1}(U) for an open U
references.context: Topology: inverse image of open subset under continuous underlying scheme map

references.phrase: suffices to test affine opens of S
references.disposition: Affine opens give a local base for this quasi-compactness condition; do not assume every open is affine.

items.review_rationale: Read the equality of Krull dimensions of all irreducible components, distinguishing dimensions of irreducible components from equality of local dimensions at all points.

references.phrase: Krull dimension of a topological space

references.disposition: The quantifier ranges over irreducible components, not all closed subsets or arbitrary neighbourhoods.

items.review_rationale: Examined supremum over lengths of strict finite chains of irreducible closed subsets and the special empty-space dimension convention. The chain entries need not be irreducible components.

references.phrase: strict finite chain of irreducible closed subsets
references.context: Order theory and topology: inclusion chain of distinct irreducible closed subspaces with integer length

references.phrase: supremum and dimension −∞ for empty space
references.disposition: The dimension is a supremum of finite chain lengths with a separate convention for the empty space, not a maximum guaranteed to exist.
